explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest not only on the money you first save but also on the interest that has already been added.

evidence.quote: Compound interest: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: For example, $1,000 at 5 percent compounded once a year grows to $1,050 after one year and to $1,102.50 after two years, because the second year interest is calculated on $1,050.

evidence.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).
After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.

explanations.text: Starting to save early in an account that pays interest allows money to grow faster through the effect of compound interest.

evidence.quote: The sooner you start saving in an account that pays interest, the faster your money can grow.
The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education, the faster your money can grow from compound interest.
